events.title: Summary judgment ruling — Oregon Environmental Council v. Internal Revenue Service (D.D.C.) 1:25-cv-04400
events.summary: Judge Kollar-Kotelly granted Plaintiffs' motion for summary judgment, holding that IRS Notice 2025-42 - which eliminated the “Five Percent Safe Harbor” test as a means of establishing the “beginning of construction” for wind and large-scale solar projects seeking clean electricity tax credits under 26 U.S.C. §§ 45Y and 48E - was arbitrary and capricious under the APA, 5 U.S.C. § 706(2)(A), because the agency failed to articulate a reasoned explanation for the change, ignored serious reliance interests engendered by more than a decade of prior guidance, and did not address alternative, less-disruptive policy options identified by commenters. The court vacated the Notice in full and remanded to the IRS for further consideration. Plaintiffs Hopi Utilities Corporation (HUC) and the Maryland Office of People's Counsel (OPC) were dismissed for lack of jurisdiction - HUC because it had access to alternative remedies under the Anti-Injunction Act, and OPC because binding precedent bars state agencies from asserting parens patriae claims against the federal government.
events.why_relevant: This litigation update changes the posture of an active legal challenge to Trump administration action.

events.summary: The Food and Drug Administration issued a final order classifying over-the-counter tests to detect SARS-CoV-2 from clinical specimens into Class II (special controls) under 21 CFR 866.3984. events.title: Summary judgment ruling — State of California v. Noem (D. Mass.) 1:25-cv-13829
events.summary: Judge Sorokin granted Plaintiffs' motion for summary judgment, holding that the $100,000 payment requirement imposed on H-1B petitions under Proclamation 10973 is an unlawful tax exceeding the President's authority under the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA), and that the agency actions implementing it violated the APA by bypassing notice-and-comment, exceeding statutory authority, and being arbitrary and capricious. In the same order, Judge Sorokin denied Defendants' motion to dismiss except as to Plaintiffs' claims against the Department of Justice, the Attorney General, the Department of Labor, and the Secretary of Labor, which Plaintiffs had agreed to voluntarily dismiss and which the court dismissed without prejudice.

events.title: Tony Terrell Clark v. Mississippi (25-6846): Certiorari denied; Sotomayor statement on Batson jury-selection standards
events.summary: The Supreme Court denied certiorari in Tony Terrell Clark's capital case, in which he challenged his conviction on grounds of ineffective assistance of counsel during Batson jury-selection proceedings. Justice Sotomayor issued a statement criticizing the Mississippi Supreme Court's standard for evaluating Batson claims in the context of ineffective-assistance-of-counsel claims. She argued that Mississippi's requirement that a defendant prove a competently presented Batson challenge would have changed the trial outcome is inconsistent with Batson's structural-error status and foundational principles protecting against racial discrimination in jury selection. Sotomayor noted that Clark's prosecution struck Black prospective jurors at more than five times the rate of white jurors and applied a double standard in evaluating juror fitness.
events.why_relevant: Denial of certiorari in a capital case involving racial discrimination in jury selection, coupled with a Justice's statement criticizing state court standards for evaluating such claims, signals unresolved constitutional tension regarding the protection of defendants' rights to racially nondiscriminatory jury selection and the proper standard for evaluating ineffective assistance in that context.
events.federal_nexus: Supreme Court review of state capital conviction; federal constitutional question regarding Batson v. Kentucky and Sixth Amendment right to effective assistance of counsel.
events.basis: During Clark's capital trial, the prosecution struck Black prospective jurors at a rate more than five times that of white jurors... the Mississippi Supreme Court's approach, to the extent it requires a criminal defendant to show that a competently presented Batson challenge would have produced a different trial outcome, is almost certainly wrong.

events.summary: Environmental and environmental-justice organizations filed a complaint in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia challenging the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service's approval of the "Boca Chica Land Exchange," which would transfer 715 acres of wildlife corridor lands in the Lower Rio Grande Valley National Wildlife Refuge to SpaceX in exchange for 683 acres of private land. events.title: Senate Energy Committee advanced Wildfire Prevention Act with Roadless Rule repeal amendment
events.summary: On June 11, the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, chaired by Mike Lee, voted 11–9 along party lines to advance the Wildfire Prevention Act with a last-minute amendment repealing the 2001 Roadless Rule. events.title: Louisiana jury awards $1.1bn in damages to abuse survivor under lookback law
events.summary: A Bossier Parish jury awarded Pamela Lockridge $1.1bn in damages for childhood sexual abuse by her late stepfather Leroy Edwards between 1962 and 1976. The verdict—comprising $500m for pain and suffering, $600m in punitive damages, and $585,000 for medical/psychological expenses—was rendered under Louisiana's 2021 "lookback law," which temporarily eliminated filing deadlines for historical child molestation cases. Edwards had admitted the abuse to authorities in 2011 but could not be criminally prosecuted due to statute of limitations; Lockridge's original 2012 civil suit was dismissed before the lookback law's passage and constitutional validation in 2024.
events.why_relevant: The verdict demonstrates how legislative reform (the lookback law) restored access to justice for long-silenced abuse survivors, expanding the capacity of courts to hold perpetrators accountable and signaling institutional recognition of historical wrongs.
events.basis: A north-west Louisiana jury recently awarded a staggering $1.1bn in damages to a woman who sued over childhood sexual molestation at the hands of her late stepfather in the 1960s and 1970s.
